title: Burmese/Myanmar language and alphabet
at_a_glance: Native name: မြန်မာဘာသာ [mjəmà bàðà]
notable_features: Type of writing system: Abugida / Syllabic Alphabet - each letter has an inherent vowel, which is pronounced [a̰] or [ə] [a]. Other vowels sounds are indicated using separate letters or diacritics which appear above, below, in front of, after or around the consonant.
Writing direction: left to right in horizontal lines.
Script family: Proto-Sinaitic, Phoenician, Aramaic, Brāhmī, Tamil-Brahmi, Pallava, Burmese
Used to write: Aiton, Akha, Arakanese, Burmese, Eastern Pwo Karen, Jingpho, Khamti, Marma, Pali, Palaung, Pa'O, S'gaw Karen, Tai Laing, Tai Phake, Western Pwo

The rounded appearance of letters is a result of the use of palm leaves as the traditional writing material. Straight lines would have torn the leaves. The Burmese name for the script is ca-lonh 'round script'.
